mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-72.0 to -64.6), indicating self-reinforcing momentum as consumers resume discretionary shopping habits; this trend should persist into the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -72.0 at t-2w to -64.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the observed three-week upward momentum.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, it signals renewed commuting and errand-running capacity that mechanically feeds retail footfall, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -64.3 at t-2w to -59.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after TRANSIT meets the trigger condition in two consecutive weekly observations.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous upward movement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a joint commuting-and-work recovery that compounds retail footfall more strongly than either series alone, producing an amplified rise in RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than growth predicted from either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (20.0 to 17.4) signals reduced time spent at home, consistent with behavioral loosening during a reopening regime, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks; in a tightening regime this relationship would reverse or vanish.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 20.0 at t-2w to 17.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks despite continued RESIDENTIAL decline, or the relationship inverts under a tightening-restrictions regime.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rise in PARKS mobility exceeding 5 points is a proxy for policy easing of outdoor and public-space restrictions, which typically precedes relaxed retail capacity limits and higher RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -63.7 at t-2w to -58.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS jump exceeding 5 points, indicating the proxy does not capture policy easing.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-February cold weather suppresses outdoor activity, reflected in relatively low PARKS values; this seasonal cold drives substitution toward indoor retail and recreation venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people shift activity indoors rather than reducing total mobility.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 5 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC does not decline concurrently
evidence_refs: fact:decision point is mid-February, a winter month
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS move in the same direction over the next four weeks, contradicting the hypothesized indoor-substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility near its recent range indicates steady essential-shopping behavior that anchors consumer routines, serving as a floor that supports a modest continued rise in RETAIL_REC over the next week as discretionary spending resumes alongside essential trips.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -39.4 at t-2w to -31.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable or improving, indicating no anchoring effect.

mechanism_narrative: If both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT simultaneously decline week-on-week, this co-movement signals renewed tightening of restrictions (e.g., reduced capacity limits or advisories), which would drag RETAIL_REC lower over the following four weeks as discretionary trips are curtailed first.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both fall week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both series showed declines between t-3w and t-2w before recovering
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next four weeks following simultaneous drops in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT, or it rises instead.
